note.title: Separation techniques — filtration and distillation
note.overview: Choose and explain filtration or distillation for separating mixtures, linking each method to solubility, particle state and boiling point.
learningGoals: Recall the core knowledge and vocabulary for Separation techniques — filtration and distillation.
Explain or produce the answer independently rather than relying only on recognition.
Apply the idea accurately to a new prompt and check every required detail.
mustMemoriseRules: filtration → a method separating an insoluble solid from a liquid
residue → the insoluble solid remaining on filter paper
filtrate → the liquid that passes through filter paper
simple distillation → a method used to obtain a solvent from a solution or separate liquids with sufficiently different boiling points
lower-boiling component → the component that vaporises first during distillation
condenser → apparatus that cools vapour so it changes back into liquid
fractional distillation → separation of a mixture of liquids using different boiling points and a fractionating column
fractionating column → apparatus enabling repeated evaporation and condensation to improve liquid separation
crystallisation → partly evaporating solvent to concentrate a solution and cooling it so crystals form
avoiding complete dryness → not heating some dissolved substances until all solvent is gone because heat may damage them

detailedExplanation: Verified against The Tiffin Girls’ School Year 9 Chemistry Curriculum Outline 2026–27 (AQA GCSE Chemistry 8462).
Filtration separates an insoluble solid from a liquid. The liquid and dissolved substances pass through the filter paper as the filtrate, while the insoluble solid remains as the residue.

Simple distillation separates a solvent from a solution by using differences in boiling point. The mixture is heated so the more volatile liquid evaporates; the vapour is cooled in a condenser and collected as the distillate.
A strong method explanation names the physical property that makes the separation possible, rather than only listing apparatus.

additionalSourceSections.body:
Filtration: insoluble solid + liquid → residue stays on filter paper; filtrate passes through.
Simple distillation: heat solution → lower-boiling liquid evaporates → vapour cools in condenser → liquid distillate collected.
Choose the method from the physical property being used.
